subject: History
question_text: What were the main factors that led to the subsistence crisis in France during the Old Regime?
expected_answer: The subsistence crisis occurred due to rapid population growth from 23 million to 28 million, leading to high demand for food grains. Production of grains could not keep pace with demand, so the price of bread rose rapidly. Wages of workers did not increase with prices, widening the gap between rich and poor. Frequent drought or hail reduced harvests further.

marking_rubric.point: Rapid population growth (23M to 28M) leading to increased demand for food grains
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for mentioning population surge and rising food demand
acceptable_alternatives: Demand for food grains outstripping production
common_misconceptions: Thinking famine was caused purely by foreign war

marking_rubric.point: Inflation of bread prices and fixed wages widening economic disparity
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for bread price hike and wage stagnation
acceptable_alternatives: Prices of staple food rose sharply while workers' wages remained fixed
Widening gap between the rich and the poor

marking_rubric.point: Adverse weather conditions like drought or hail destroying harvests
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for bad weather / natural disasters damaging crop yields
acceptable_alternatives: Severe drought or hail damaging harvest yields
Agricultural failure due to bad weather

subject: History
question_text: Explain the circumstances that led to the Tennis Court Oath and the formation of the National Assembly in 1789.
expected_answer: Louis XVI convened the Estates-General on 5 May 1789 to pass proposals for new taxes. Each estate had one vote, but the Third Estate demanded that each member have one vote. When the King rejected this democratic principle, representatives of the Third Estate walked out. On 20 June 1789, they assembled in the indoor tennis court at Versailles under the leadership of Mirabeau and Abbé Sieyès, declared themselves the National Assembly, and swore not to disperse until they had drafted a constitution limiting royal power.

marking_rubric.point: Convening of the Estates-General on 5 May 1789 and the dispute over voting procedure
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for mentioning the Estates-General meeting and voting rules dispute
acceptable_alternatives: King called Estates General; dispute over one estate one vote vs one person one vote
common_misconceptions: Confusing Estates-General with the National Assembly

marking_rubric.point: Third Estate's demand for democratic voting (each member having one vote)
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for democratic voting demand based on Rousseau's philosophy
acceptable_alternatives: Third Estate wanted voting per head rather than per estate

marking_rubric.point: Walkout and assembly at the indoor tennis court of Versailles on 20 June 1789
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for the date (20 June 1789) and tennis court venue
acceptable_alternatives: Third estate walked out in protest and gathered in Versailles tennis hall
common_misconceptions: Believing the oath took place in Paris

marking_rubric.point: Declaration of the National Assembly and the oath not to disperse without a constitution
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for self-proclamation as National Assembly and drafting pledge
acceptable_alternatives: Swearing an oath to frame a constitution that would curtail monarch's power
common_misconceptions: Thinking the oath was to execute the King

marking_rubric.point: Leadership provided by Mirabeau (noble) and Abbé Sieyès (priest)
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for naming leaders Mirabeau and Abbé Sieyès
acceptable_alternatives: Led by Mirabeau who gave speeches and Abbé Sieyès who wrote 'What is the Third Estate'
common_misconceptions: Naming Robespierre as the primary leader of the Tennis Court Oath

subject: History
chapter: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
question_text: What were the main demands included in Vladimir Lenin's 'April Theses'?
expected_answer: In April 1917, Vladimir Lenin returned to Russia from exile and put forward three key demands known as the 'April Theses': 1. The war (First World War) be brought to a close; 2. Land be transferred to the peasants; 3. Banks be nationalized.

marking_rubric.point: First World War be brought to an immediate close / exit from war
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for stopping the war
acceptable_alternatives: Immediate withdrawal of Russia from World War I
common_misconceptions: Thinking Lenin wanted to expand the war

marking_rubric.point: Land be transferred to the peasants
marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for redistribution of land to peasants
acceptable_alternatives: Confiscation of landlord estates and redistribution to farmers
common_misconceptions: Thinking land was to be privatized into corporate farms

marking_rubric.description: Award 1 mark for state control / nationalisation of banks
acceptable_alternatives: Banks be brought under government/soviet control
common_misconceptions: Believing banks were to remain privately owned
